author: B

components.title: Sum and compare units by product
components.what: Aggregate units for each product across all orders regardless of status, calculate the totals (Anvil 120, Easel 94, Dowel 81, Crate 30, Bolt 26), compare them, and select the product with the largest total.

log.author: B
log.draft:
Summing the `units` column for each product across all rows, regardless of `status`:

Anvil = 34+30+6+26+15+9 = 120  
Easel = 9+14+34+37 = 94  
Dowel = 36+8+37 = 81  
Crate = 9+21 = 30  
Bolt = 11+8+7 = 26  

The largest total is Anvil.

FINAL: Anvil

asked: How did you verify that every one of the 18 data rows was assigned to exactly one product group (row counts per product summing to 18), and can you state those per-product row counts?

Since the question says 'regardless of status', did you confirm that the cancelled and pending rows (ORD-1055, ORD-1156, ORD-1633, ORD-1232, ORD-1059) were included in the totals, and would the winner change if they had been excluded?
replies: I counted the product entries across all 18 data rows: Anvil 6, Easel 4, Dowel 3, Crate 2, and Bolt 3. These row counts sum to 6+4+3+2+3 = 18, so every row was assigned to exactly one product group.

Yes. The five pending or cancelled rows were included: ORD-1055 (Bolt, 8), ORD-1156 (Anvil, 15), ORD-1633 (Anvil, 26), ORD-1232 (Anvil, 30), and ORD-1059 (Easel, 34). If excluded, the totals would be Anvil 49, Easel 60, Dowel 81, Crate 30, and Bolt 18, so the winner would change to Dowel. The original answer is correct because the question specifies counting all statuses.
